Senses.Explanation: To transmit mind by mind is a lineage formula contrasted with transmission through language or written teachings. Hongren tells Huineng that the teaching is transmitted mind by mind and each person is made to awaken and understand for himself. Xuefeng Yicun joins Bodhidharma's arrival, mind-by-mind transmission, and not setting up written words. Dahui Zonggao says that the old sages had no transmission by language and spoke only of this. Huangbo Xiyun says that deliberating mind already misses and that transmitting mind by mind is the correct view. The Chan Gate Treasury Record explicitly calls it Bodhidharma's saying and has Bodhidharma answer Huike's question about written teaching-canons by pairing it again with not setting up written words. Tiantong Xianjie supplies the corrective witness: transmitting mind by mind makes the disease turn deeper. The record therefore preserves the lineage claim, its contrast with language and writing, and a named criticism of the same formula.
Senses.Note: The exact phrase has 110 hits in 56 allowlisted texts. Six anchors across five works meet the frequency floor. Affirmation, historical attribution, contrast, and criticism all deploy the same transmission formula and do not justify separate senses.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Combined Essentials of the Five Lamps (聯燈會要), section on Xuefeng Yicun: Xuefeng joins Bodhidharma's arrival from the west, transmission mind by mind, and not setting up written words.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: In his Recorded Sayings (大慧普覺禪師語錄), instruction to Layman Zhitong, Dahui Zonggao says the old sages had no transmission by language and spoke only of transmitting mind by mind.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Chan Gate Treasury Record (禪門寶藏錄) records Bodhidharma answering Huike that his teaching transmits mind by mind and does not set up written words; the preceding narration explicitly attributes the formula to Bodhidharma.
